topic: What beamforming strategies optimally balance implementation complexity and SINR enhancement when satellite transmitters employ MRT despite imperfect CSI?
consensus_response: The optimal beamforming strategy to balance implementation complexity and Signal-to-Interference-plus-Noise Ratio (SINR) enhancement in satellite transmitters employing Maximum Ratio Transmission (MRT) despite imperfect Channel State Information (CSI) is hybrid beamforming. This approach combines analog and digital processing to create robust and efficient precoding matrices, mitigating SINR degradation caused by CSI estimation errors. Hybrid beamforming leverages the strengths of each method, balancing implementation complexity and performance, while reducing the cost of inaccurate precoding matrices.
reference_context: In multibeam satellite systems, aggressive frequency reuse schemes have shown to be promising for spectrally efficient high-throughput wireless communications. Linear precoding techniques manage interferences by exploiting spatial degrees of freedom, but their incorporation is inhibited by inherent satellite system characteristics.
